correctness.rationale: Frozen RESULT.md line 28 labels a matrix U^TPU but incorrectly gives diagonal 1+m/2; that is the diagonal of I+U^TPU. The complete corrected RESULT.md in repairs/1 corrects the identity and supplies its derivation and the Gram-matrix calculation; the original is unchanged. From g=Pb_0 and g_{j+m}=-g_j one obtains b_0^TPb_0=m/2 and b_t^TPb_0=(m-2t)/2. The cross-correlation S_t satisfies 2S_t-S_{t-1}-S_{t+1}=(m-2t)/2 and S_0=-S_m=m(m^2+2)/24, which uniquely gives the displayed cubic. Consequently the determinant factor is m+1+x and the Woodbury trace gives the stated rational gain. The derivative of the gain is strictly positive, so the discrete maximum of t(m-t) gives both optimizer sets including m=2 and both parities. Substitution of x=m-1 and x=m^2/4+O(1) gives the three stated asymptotics. An independently written grounded-Laplacian calculation matched both formulas and both optimizer sets for every admissible t at 2<=m<=9; see branches/625f4f20-8b81-4afa-8ed1-6b8315f4001e/independent_check.py. The finite check does not replace the proof. Frozen check.py and VERIFICATION.md were inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: Two diameters are natural longest shortcuts on a unit cycle. Their relative separation changes the exact objectives; the result identifies the full set of common optimizers, and the resistance gain has a factor-of-two separation from adjacent diameters in the leading term while the tree-count ratio grows with size. This is a concrete two-objective benchmark, not simply evaluation of the general matrix identities or a claim about unrestricted augmentation. The proof repair leaves that value intact.
